title: Senate Floor Debate
subtitle: S.2780 — Defending America's Cyber Infrastructure Act

metadata.laymanSummary: The Senate voted to strengthen federal defenses against cyberattacks on critical infrastructure like power grids, water systems, and financial networks.

data.billTitle: Defending America's Cyber Infrastructure Act — Strengthening federal cyber defenses against state-sponsored attacks

speakers.name: Sen. Roger Wicker
speakers.title: R-MS · Senate Armed Services Chair
speakers.quote: China and Russia are probing our power grid, our water systems, and our financial networks every single day. This is not a hypothetical threat. This bill gives CISA the resources and authority to defend America in the cyber domain before the lights go out.

speakers.name: Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse
speakers.title: D-RI · Senate Judiciary
speakers.quote: This is rare bipartisan action that our national security demands. Cyberattacks on American infrastructure do not ask for your party registration. I urge every colleague to support this legislation.

speakers.name: Sen. Rand Paul
speakers.title: R-KY · Senate
speakers.quote: This bill expands government surveillance of private networks under the guise of cybersecurity. We should be cautious about giving federal agencies unprecedented access to private sector systems. Liberty requires that we ask hard questions even about bills with good intentions.

data.title: What This Vote Means
data.text: S.2780 passed the Senate 67-32 with bipartisan support. It allocates $4.2 billion to CISA for cyber defense programs, mandates 48-hour breach reporting for critical infrastructure operators, and authorizes offensive cyber operations against state-sponsored attack networks. The bill now moves to the House.

data.title: Should the federal government have greater authority over private sector cyber defenses?
